title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §5, 'Les groupes M_{ρ,σ}, M^♭_{ρ,σ} (via N_{ρ,σ})', in the post-Longue-Marche manuscript. The setting appears to be the Teichmüller / Galois–Teichmüller material. M_0 is a rank-2 lattice generated by λ_0, λ_1, with λ_∞ = −λ_0 − λ_1. This looks like the abelianised loop classes of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. ρ and σ are automorphisms. N_{ρ,σ} is a group (scheme) of pairs (α,β) satisfying a compatibility relation with ρ and σ. The previous page computed that the inner automorphisms int(l) compatible with the relation are exactly those with l = c_0 λ_0. That gives the rank-one subgroup L_0^M = Im(Z → M), n ↦ nλ_0, and a homomorphism (121) L_0^{M_0} (≅ G_a?) → N_{ρ,σ}, together with a map L_0^M → G^+.

On this page Grothendieck checks the hypotheses of the standard pushout-of-extensions construction:
(i) The image of L_0 in N_{ρ,σ} is normal (invariant).
(ii) The map u: L_0^M → G^+ is N_{ρ,σ}-equivariant. N acts on L_0 through μ, and on G^+ ⊃ M ⊃ L_0^M.
(iii) The two actions of L_0^M on G^+ coincide: one restricted from the N-action, the other inner via u.

'By the general nonsense' one then gets a group scheme M_{ρ,σ} = (G^+ ⋊ N_{ρ,σ}) / {(u(l)^{-1}, l)}. It sits in a morphism of extensions (123):
- top row 1 → L_0^M → N_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1, with Γ_{ρ,σ} := N_{ρ,σ}/L_0^M;
- bottom row 1 → G^+ → M_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1;
- the map on Γ is the identity.

Doing the same with G^+ replaced by the subgroup M gives the extension (124): 1 → M → M^♮_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1. There is a morphism (124) → (123) and an inclusion (125) M^♮_{ρ,σ} ⊂ M_{ρ,σ}. A marginal note reconciles notation with §49 VI: the group called M_{ρ,σ} here would there be written M_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ, and M^♮ similarly (loc. cit. p. 80).

The next page goes on to analyse Γ_{ρ,σ} through its 'connected' part Γ^{0+}, a rank computation of N^{0+} as a Z-module. The purpose is to construct groups M_{ρ,σ} (presumably automorphism or Teichmüller-type groups attached to a pair of symmetries ρ, σ) as extensions of a discrete quotient Γ_{ρ,σ} by G^+ or by M.
errors: No mathematical error. The three conditions listed (normality of the image, equivariance of u, agreement of the two L-actions on G^+) are exactly what the pushout of a group extension along a homomorphism requires.
There is a notational inconsistency: the section title on the previous page announces M^♭_{ρ,σ}, while (124)/(125) use a symbol read as M^♮ (or M^G).
The superscript in (122), 'L_0^{Ma}', is presumably L_0^{M_0} or L_0^M, in line with (121).
The page asserts that (121) is compatible with the actions but does not verify it here; the verification is left implicit.

ideas.what: Pushout of a group (scheme) extension 1→L→N→Γ→1 along an equivariant homomorphism L→G, whose inner action matches the restricted action, giving 1→G→M→Γ→1
ideas.modern_name: pushout / induced extension (change of band) in nonabelian group extension theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Schreier, Eilenberg–MacLane); Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne for the topos version
ideas.where_published: Generally used in the SGA framework (e.g. SGA 7 exposé on extensions) and in Giraud's work done under Grothendieck

ideas.what: Comparison of the extensions obtained by pushing along M ⊂ G^+, giving M^♮_{ρ,σ} ⊂ M_{ρ,σ}
Groups M_{ρ,σ} attached to a pair of automorphisms ρ, σ, in the Teichmüller / Galois–Teichmüller context of the Longue Marche continuation
ideas.modern_name: possibly related to normalisers/centralisers of finite-order elements in Teichmüller-type groups (unclear)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981, unpublished manuscript) – unsure whether this specific construction appears

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine technical step: it checks the hypotheses of the standard pushout of a group extension, then defines groups via the resulting morphism of extensions. The ambient objects (N_{ρ,σ}, G^+, Γ_{ρ,σ}) belong to an unpublished development, but nothing on this page is a new idea or result in itself.
transcription_corrections: 'L_0^{M_0} ≃ G_0' is probably '≃ G_a', matching (121) on the previous page.
The bottom-left group in (123), 'G^{+a}', is presumably just G^+ with a stray mark.
Marginal note, roughly: 'avec les notations du §49 VI, le groupe noté ici M_{ρ,σ} serait sans doute noté M_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ, et M^♮_{ρ,σ} serait noté M^♮_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ (loc. cit. 80)'.
In (124) the left entry of the bottom row is M; a crossed-out symbol precedes it.
'd'après les topos généraux' may be 'd'après les trucs/généralités générales'; the reading is uncertain.
